humanities_role_explanation: Comic images (AI-generated comics and Manga109 pages) supply the items, but the competence tested is general MLLM cultural awareness (visual recognition, conflict detection, translation), not a humanities discipline such as comics studies.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Comic page images (Doubao-generated comics and Manga109 pages) paired with text questions/prompts; Generation@Culture gives a source Japanese sentence plus the comic page.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Q1 background culture identification (multi-answer multiple choice), Q2 culture-aware object detection (choose the option listing exactly the objects), Q3 yes/no identification of cultural conflict, Q4 free-form description of conflicts ('Something should not be in Some Culture'), and Q5 Japanese-to-EN/DE/RU/TH/ES machine translation called 'Culturally-aligned Content Generation'.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to cultural awareness of MLLMs using comics, though with three tasks; not a broad general-purpose benchmark.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: 11 open-source MLLMs: SPHINX, Monkey, MiniGPT-v2, mPLUG-Owl3, LLaVA1.5-7B, LLaVA-NeXT, LLaVA-OV, InternLM-XC2.5, Llama3.2, Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL2.

quantitative_metrics.note: Accuracy, composite CACC, BLEU, COMET, BLEURT; also CDPI/CBI/CAD diversity measures.

summary: The paper introduces C3B, a comic-based multicultural, multitask and multilingual benchmark of 2,220 images and 18,789 QA pairs spanning culture-aware object extraction, cultural-conflict detection, and culturally-aligned translation. Eleven open-source MLLMs are evaluated and fall well below human performance, especially on conflict understanding and lesser-known cultures.
key_findings: Qwen2.5-VL is best overall (Q1 ACC 53.7, CACC 34.2; BLEU 13.2 on JA-EN). Models score extremely low on Q4 ACC (max 3.87). Humans outperform models across all tiers (e.g. Q1 92.0 vs 48.0 on easy questions). Lesser-known cultures (Finnish, Somali) have higher error rates than well-known ones (Cambodia, Japan). JA-TH is the hardest translation pair and JA-EN the easiest.
facets_explanation: Culture and object lists were manually annotated (undergraduates then graduate-student review, IAA 76.8%). Conflict@Culture answers were produced by DeepSeek-V3 then manually verified, and Generation@Culture reference translations (16,743 of 18,789 QA pairs) were produced by a DeepSeek translator-reviewer multi-agent pipeline with manual verification. Q1 allows 1-5 correct options, hence an answer set. Disagreement is treated as an error to be resolved by group discussion.
results_explanation: Best headline: Qwen2.5-VL 'Q1 (ACC) 53.7' in Table 3. Human baseline on easy Q1 is 92.0 vs model 48.0 in Table 7; human gap computed as the difference between the easy-tier human Q1 ACC (92.0) and the Q1 best model ACC 53.7 in Table 3 (about 38), while 44 is the easy-tier human-minus-model gap of 92.0-48.0 (Table 7 averages models). Format gap exists via Q4 ACC vs CACC and easy/hard tiers, but no single point value is given as a gap comparison.

humanities_role.quote: C3B is a novel comic-centric benchmark designed to comprehensively evaluate MLLMs’ cultural awareness capabilities.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: We adhered strictly to the official inference example codes provided by the respective model developers.

gold_source.quote: we manually inspect all generated results
we employed DeepSeek-V3 as the base model

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: This task requires the MLLM not only to identify objects within the image but also to understand whether or not the object is related to a specific cultural context.

answer_multiplicity.quote: In Q1, the number of correct numbers ranges from 1 to 5 among 5 candidate options.

plurality_treatment.quote: In cases where inaccuracies were identified, the annotations were revised based on the outcomes of group discussions.

reported_format_gap.quote: ACC refers to the accuracy of Q4 calculated without referencing answers to Q1 and Q2.

reported_cultural_asymmetry.quote: representative cultures (e.g., Cambodia and Japan) are reliably identified, while lesser-known cultures (e.g., Finnish and Somalia) exhibit notably higher error rates.
